# codex-run-1: SourceTrace run by OpenAI Codex

The first run of SourceTrace by an agent other than Claude, on the same inputs as the Claude runs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Agent | OpenAI Codex, run by the project owner on 2026-11-05 (model version not recorded) |
| Skill | v0.2.0 (commit `8c88b42`), including the third rule revision, which no run had used before |
| Inputs | `images/` and `knowledge-tree.json` of this test set, copied into a clean folder outside the repository, so earlier runs and reviews were not visible (but see the first attempt below) |
| Prompt | The same request as the Claude runs, plus a question on how the images were read |

## A first attempt in the wrong folder

Before this run, Codex was started once in the repository folder instead of the clean run folder (about 09:10). There, `../input/` does not exist, so `validate_input.py` reported two `FILE_NOT_FOUND` errors. Codex did what SKILL.md says:
- it stopped at stage 1;
- it did not look for another test set to audit instead;
- it wrote a `skill-feedback.md` explaining the failure.

By its own account, it read only the skill's files. Its feedback is kept as [first-attempt-skill-feedback.md](first-attempt-skill-feedback.md).

## Did Codex follow the skill?

Yes, with no help.

- **Scripts:** it ran all three scripts. `validate_evidence.py` ran twice, because Codex refined its diagram transcriptions after enlarging two figures; both runs passed. `build_report.py` passed on the first try.
- **Images:** it read the 12 images with its `view_image` tool. It cropped and enlarged two small diagrams with Pillow to check details: the Titanic tree thresholds and the Bayesian-network arrows.
- **Uncertain evidence:** one unreadable decimal was recorded as `low` certainty and not used to reject anything.
- **Report:** generated by the script, not written by hand. The saved `report.md` and `audit.json` rebuild byte for byte with the current `build_report.py`.
- **Paths:** the new relative image paths resolve, both in the run folder and in this saved copy.

| **Match** | | **5/18** | **15/18** | **15/18** |

("detail" is `unsupported-expansion` with scope `detail`.)

- **What Codex fixed:** all three items Claude run 2 got wrong (N027, E004, N008). These are the cases the second revision targeted, so this is the first sign that the revision works. It comes from a different agent, though, so the rules and the agent can't be told apart.
- **What Codex missed:**
  - N006 and N024: it accepted "区分系统性偏离与对训练数据的敏感程度" and "学习数据表示" as explanations of the term. The owner judged them added details. The "explanation of the term" rule from the second revision may now be applied too widely.
  - N017: it marked "尽量保留重要信息" as an added detail, where the owner judged the whole definition unverifiable. It is low risk in both readings.
- **Unreviewed items:** Codex agrees with Claude run 2 on every one of the other 80 items, including the two edges both flag (E020, E056).

## Omissions: the main difference

| | Claude run 1 | Claude run 2 | Codex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Omissions | 25 (11 core, 14 supporting) | 25 (10 core, 15 supporting) | **44 (29 core, 15 supporting)** |
| Risk: high / medium / low | 1 / 12 / 27 | 0 / 13 / 28 | 0 / 31 / 26 |

The difference is granularity, not different content:

- **Bare list items:** Codex reported each model in the article's model list as its own core omission (F-020 to F-032, F-034), for example "线性判别分析", "最近邻居法", "蒙特卡罗方法". The list only names them. The Claude runs reported the list's grouping as one omission. Codex explained its choice in [skill-feedback.md](skill-feedback.md): it treated the list as an overview, whose topics are core under the rules.
- **Illustrations:** the Titanic figure (F-035) and the Rain/Sprinkler figure (F-038) illustrate concepts that are already in the tree. The Claude runs treated them as not knowledge.
- **Headings past the cut-off:** the 软件 heading at the bottom of page 12 (F-042) starts the section where the capture ends.

The owner has not judged the omissions of any wiki-ml-zh run, so which granularity is right is still open. The rules do not settle it: "One omission per missing concept" and "a topic in an agenda/overview slide is core" pull in different directions for a long list of bare names.

## Not recorded

- Codex model version, token use and time. The output files were written between about 09:14 and 09:29, so roughly 15 minutes.
- Codex's two enlarged diagram crops (`image-inspection/`) were not saved here.
